villagepax.quest.maya_founding_2: The terrace is slipping after the rains. We need stone, a lot of it, or the field will go down with the harvest.
villagepax.quest.maya_founding_3: You are no stranger to us. Feed the village, and I will hand you a town hall blueprint: found your own settlement.

villagepax.greeting.book_hover: A book with what you need in the first hour
villagepax.guide.given: The wayfarer's notes are in your hands.
villagepax.guide.what:
Village Pax

Somewhere stand villages not your own: their houses, their fields, their trade.

You have nothing yet — but the right to come and speak.
villagepax.guide.find:
Find a village

It may stand hundreds of blocks away, and only in its own biome.

Ask the way:
/villagepax locate
villagepax.guide.elder:
The elder

Click him. He will name an errand: logs, stone, food.

Bring it and click again. Trust is shown in the same window.
villagepax.guide.blueprint:
The blueprint

The third errand hands you the town hall blueprint.

Place it on level solid ground and the colony is yours — with its first citizen, a builder.
villagepax.guide.console:
The colony console

Click your town hall.

Citizens, food, beds and building are there, and there you hand out crafts: builder, courier, farmer, lumberjack, guard.
villagepax.guide.order:
Marking a building

Stand where you want it and press "Mark".

It will face you. A ghost shows the footprint before the first block.
villagepax.guide.storage:
Storage

Put what the building needs into the town hall chest.

The courier carries, the builder lays. If something is missing, the chat says what.
villagepax.guide.citizens:
Citizens

A new one arrives when there is a free bed and food in storage.

A hungry colony empties: first a warning, then they leave.
villagepax.guide.trade:
Trade

The elder keeps a stall.

The coin is our own: copper, silver, gold — nine to one. A purse carries them for you.
villagepax.guide.trust:
Trust

A friend buys cheaper and sells dearer.

It grows with errands, trade and gifts. Give what the village buys, and no more than once a day.
villagepax.guide.people:
The people

Word travels past one village: a favour to one reaches the whole people — and their rivals the other way.

See the "People" tab.
villagepax.guide.caravan:
Caravans

A village that counts you a friend sends a merchant with a cart.

He stands a day by your hall. You may rob him — but everyone will know.
villagepax.guide.raid:
The sword

A killed villager and a robbed caravan cost trust.

Let it fall too low and they will come armed. You get a day's warning. Hand someone the guard's craft before that.
villagepax.guide.peace:
Peace

You can cut down those who come, but it does not make peace.

Only what broke it can mend it: gifts and deeds.

villagepax.screen.faith.no_pantheon: This people prays to no one.

villagepax.guide.faith:
§lFaith§r

Build a temple and an altar will stand in it. Put on it what your people's gods take: grain, stone, iron. What you offer decides who you pray to.

A god takes one offering a day, and that is for a long while. But then: a blessing for three days, a miracle in the black hour, and at the Kept tier — a gift found nowhere else.
villagepax.quest.lumberjack_1: I fell trees faster than the grove grows. Bring me saplings and I'll plant for us both.
villagepax.quest.lumberjack_2: The soil here is mean; an oak takes ten years. Give me bone meal and it'll stand in a week. And I'll put in a word for you with the Sower.
villagepax.quest.guard_1: They come out of the woods at night. We have bows and nothing to put on them.
villagepax.quest.guard_2: For blades. The mountain is far and our smith has no iron. Bring some and I'll give you my old shield — it saved me three times.
villagepax.quest.guard_3: Words are words, gates are gates. Raise a tower of your own and put a man on it. Do that and I'll send you my youngest — he's outgrown this place.
villagepax.quest.brewer_1: Ale without sweetness is bitter water. Cane grows by the river, and the river is a day away.
villagepax.quest.brewer_2: I can brew it; I've nothing to pour it into. Bring bottles — the first four are yours.
villagepax.quest.brewer_3: The craft is in the hands, not the barrel. Set up a cauldron of your own and I'll send an apprentice to finish his learning on your barley.
villagepax.quest.maya_weaver_1: The spider spins better than I do, and asks less. Bring me thread and I'll weave you cloth.
villagepax.quest.maya_weaver_2: White wool takes dye the way lime takes ochre. Three bolts will be yours.
villagepax.quest.maya_weaver_3: Have a loom and you'll have a weaver. Raise a weavery and I'll let my sister go — she spins straighter than I do and has nothing here for her hands.
villagepax.quest.maya_farmer_1: Cacao grows in shade, and we cut our shade for terraces. Bring beans and I'll plant again.
villagepax.quest.maya_farmer_2: The upper terrace has been drying for three years. Give me meal and I'll ask the Rain-Giver for us both.
villagepax.quest.maya_guard_1: A shaft without a feather flies where it likes. We're short of feathers — the birds left with the trees.
villagepax.quest.maya_guard_2: The gold is not for show. The Night Jaguar is given gold and sleeps easy — and an easy jaguar is an easy night.
villagepax.quest.maya_guard_3: Show me you can keep your own. Have a tower and I'll send a man — he sees in the dark better than I do.
villagepax.quest.founding_4: You have a hall and no timber. Raise a lumberjack's hut: without your own wood, winter will outlast you.
villagepax.quest.founding_5: A people that prays to no one we do not count as neighbours. Raise a temple and speak to the sky — and we will speak to you differently.
villagepax.quest.founding_6: Go to the Maya. We've been wary of them three generations and neither of us remembers why. A living man is worth more than rumour — come back and I'll let our weaver go with you.
villagepax.quest.maya_founding_4: The hall stands — and what will you eat? Break a field. Stone does not feed; earth does.
villagepax.quest.maya_founding_5: Your walls stand on someone else's earth, and the earth knows it. Lay stone on the altar and ask the Sky-Holder — then the walls will be yours.
villagepax.quest.maya_founding_6: In the north live people in white walls. They say we are savages; we say the same of them. Go and see for yourself — and when you return, take our farmer with you.
villagepax.quest.needs_colony: This is not for a man without a roof. Found your own settlement, then we'll talk.
villagepax.errand.elder: The village needs this. A small thing we can't gather ourselves.
villagepax.errand.lumberjack: My hands are on the axe. Lend me yours?
villagepax.errand.farmer: The field has its own needs, and they don't wait for autumn.
villagepax.errand.brewer: The cauldron is boiling and I'm short of something.
villagepax.errand.weaver: The loom stands idle, and that's worse than it sounds.
villagepax.errand.guard: The watch needs this. I'm not asking for myself.
villagepax.errand.builder: The work has stopped. We're short of the plainest thing.
villagepax.errand.courier: The road is long and I've nothing to set out with.
villagepax.guide.errands:
§lErrands§r

There is someone to talk to: the elder has his chain, and the woodcutter, the watchman, the brewer and the weaver have theirs. Each asks by his trade.

When a chain ends, the asking doesn't. Every trade has an errand for the day: a small thing, a coin, a grain of trust. And so every day.

Later they ask for more than goods: raise the same workplace of your own, earn a god's favour, go and meet the neighbours. And they pay with a person.
villagepax.advice.idle_hands: People sit idle while workplaces stand empty. Hand out crafts in the Citizens tab.
villagepax.advice.no_neighbours: You know no one. Find a village (/villagepax locate) and speak to its elder: they have errands, goods and blueprints.
villagepax.advice.no_temple: Your people have nowhere to go and you have no one to speak to. Raise a temple.
villagepax.advice.no_faith: The temple stands empty. Lay on the altar what the local gods take, and they will notice you.
villagepax.advice.raise_the_hall: All is running well. Raise the town hall: the next tier opens what the colony has never had.
villagepax.life.grown_up: %s has grown up and taken to work.
villagepax.life.died: %s died of old age. Days lived: %s.
villagepax.screen.assign.too_young: This is a child. They will take up a trade when they grow.
villagepax.guide.life:
§lLife§r

People age — but only on the days the colony lived before your eyes. Spend a month in a mine and no one grows older.

Two unwed adults come together on their own. A couple has children when there is a free bed and room under the population cap. A child eats and sleeps but does not work — for eight days.

An elder works at half strength and one day dies. That is no disaster: his son has already grown. If death bothers you, switch it off in config/villagepax.json.
villagepax.screen.assign.wrong_nature: %s will not take a sword — that is who they are. Give the craft to someone else.
villagepax.nature.even.what: An ordinary person: no faster and no slower than the rest.
villagepax.nature.lazy.what: Works at half strength — but endures twice as long and is the last to leave.
villagepax.nature.ambitious.what: Age is no hindrance: works at full strength even as an elder. Leaves twice as fast when unhappy.
villagepax.nature.pious.what: While the colony has an altar, carries one thing to it a day — faith grows without you.
villagepax.nature.coward.what: Will not take a sword, and flees a raider sooner and further than anyone.
villagepax.conquest.taken: Your colony has been taken: %s left without losing a single fighter. Tribute for %s days.
villagepax.conquest.took: The village of %s is taken: your war band came back whole. Tribute for %s days.
villagepax.conquest.freed: The yoke is thrown off: the war band from %s fell at your gates. The tribute ends.
villagepax.yoke.unpaid: Nothing to pay the tribute with, and %s remembers it. The treasury is empty.
villagepax.yoke.over: The tribute has run its term: %s expects nothing more.
villagepax.campaign.set_out: The war band sets out: %s swords against %s. Two days' march (%s).
villagepax.campaign.home_whole: The war band is back from %s whole: %s swords, no losses.
villagepax.campaign.home_bloodied: The war band is back from %s: %s swords, %s did not return.
villagepax.campaign.not_a_neighbour: You do not march on your own.
villagepax.campaign.no_town: Towns wage war, hamlets do not. Raise the town hall.
villagepax.campaign.no_guards: Nobody to send: a war band needs at least two guards.
villagepax.campaign.already: Your war band is already out. There is no second one.
villagepax.campaign.busy: Someone is already at that village's gates.
villagepax.campaign.besieged: There is a war band at your own gates. Deal with that first.
villagepax.campaign.too_far: Too far: the war band would never get there.
villagepax.people.screen.march_about: Or march on them: %s swords leave, and none stay behind to guard.
villagepax.screen.overview.yoke_line: The colony pays tribute to %s. Days left: %s. Beat off their next war band and it ends.
villagepax.advice.under_yoke: The colony is under tribute: silver leaves every morning. Beat off their next war band and the yoke falls.
villagepax.campaign.too_friendly: This is a friend. Friendship and war are different conversations.
villagepax.quest.pony_founding_1: We are short of rails: the herd has grown and the paddock has not. Bring spruce and we will fence it.
villagepax.quest.pony_founding_2: Winter comes and there will not be hay enough. Bring bales, and I will remember who helped.
villagepax.quest.pony_founding_3: You are no stranger now. Feed the village, and I will give you the moot hall's plan: raise your own.
villagepax.quest.pony_founding_4: Walls stand — but what will you eat? Break a paddock. Rails do not feed you; grass does.
villagepax.quest.pony_founding_5: The land does not bear on its own. Lay what you grew before the Green Mother, and she will remember you in spring.
villagepax.quest.pony_founding_6: Beyond the river live those who build in stone and look down on us. Go and speak kindly. Come back, and you take our ploughman with you.
villagepax.quest.pony_herder_1: The grain went to seed and the horses eat today. Bring wheat and I will pay in coin.
villagepax.quest.pony_herder_2: A lead breaks where the hide is thin. Bring me thick leather and I will braid one that holds a stallion.
villagepax.quest.pony_watcher_1: The flint is gone, and without it there is neither fire nor arrowhead. Bring some and I will knap it.
villagepax.quest.pony_watcher_2: Raise a lookout and watch for yourself. Raise it, and I will send you one of mine: from the saddle he sees further than you do from a roof.
